activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Eigenvectors of a 3x3 Matrix in the General Case

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -6 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 9\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}b \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vectors ${v}_{1},{v}_{2}$ shown above.
If ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are two linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3,$ what is the value of $a+b?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -6 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 9\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}-6{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+6{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are free variables. On the other hand, from the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}.$ 

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

We now deduce the eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}:$

- Since ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we must have that ${x}_{2}=0$ and ${x}_{3}=1.$ As a result, $a=0-3(1)=-3.$

- Since ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}b \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we must have that ${x}_{2}=1$ and ${x}_{3}=0.$ As a result, $b=1-3(0)=1.$

Therefore, $a+b=-3+1=-2.$
